proof_summary: The partial sums are rewritten as coefficients of \(Q(x)(1+x)^A\), with \(Q(x)=(1-x^2)/(1+x+x^2)\); expanding \((1+x)^p=1+x^p+pE_p(x)\), divisibility of \(E_p\) by \(1+x+x^2\) makes the correction coefficients anti-reciprocal, so pairing indices \(d\) and \(j-d\), a binomial-determinant factorization containing \(BY(Y-B)\), and the bound \(v_p(j!)+3\le j\) yield the required cubic gain in each scaling step. Negative parameters are reduced by a coefficient involution to the nonnegative case plus a boundary binomial term, whose analogous scaling congruence is proved by the same Frobenius-pairing method (and a perturbation for the boundary case), after which one iterates the one-step result.
